title: How Esther Ocloo Turned Ten Shillings Into Twelve Jars of Marmalade
conflicts: Starting sum: ten shillings (her 1990 CSM interview, NYT obituary, Citi Newsroom, Mental Floss) versus 'a mere sixpence' (Women's World Banking, apparently conflating her mother's sixpence) and 'a few shillings' (Al Jazeera); story uses ten, six of them spent, per her later recollection. Financing the military contract: her own 1990 account says store credit, with a bank loan only later for mechanisation after officials intervened; the NYT obituary and others say a bank lent on the contract; story follows her own account. Military customer named differently (West Africa Volunteer Forces in CSM, Royal West African Frontier Force in Wikipedia/Dictionary of African Biography); story says only 'military officers'. Year 1942 (Al Jazeera) versus 1943 (Wikipedia); story says 'early 1940s'.
notes: Stance affirms. The slate's 'a few shillings' is ten in her own account. The NYT obituary is cited via a Ghanaian newspaper's reproduction because nytimes.com returns 403. The repeat screen flagged two unrelated editions as same-founder (fuzzy match) and let it through.
